researchNotes:
SCOPE: district-run, club and university pools in Budapest, deliberately EXCLUDING the colleague's set (Komjádi, Hajós Alfréd Margitsziget, Gellért, Széchenyi, Lukács, Palatinus, Dagály, Duna Aréna, Tüskecsarnok). Research performed 2026-09-24.

METHOD. Coordinates were obtained from a single bulk OpenStreetMap Overpass query over the Budapest admin area (126 candidate features: name, lat/lon, addr:* tags, website, phone, opening_hours) and then cross-checked, one pool at a time, against the street address printed on the operator's own contact page. A coordinate was accepted ONLY when the two agreed; otherwise it would have been set null. In practice every pool retained in the set passed this check, so there are no null coordinates. Nominatim was used as a spot-check where Overpass was ambiguous (e.g. Nyéki Imre, where two nearby bus-stop nodes share the pool's name and had to be discarded).

LANE COUNTS follow the same rule and DO have nulls. A lane count was recorded only when an operator (or the operator's own schedule grid) states it in words or enumerates the lanes — 'hatpályás', '6 sávos', or a 'Sáv 1..7' header row. Where only a basin width was published, lanes were left null even when the conventional layout is obvious: an 11 m wide pool is normally 5 lanes, but that is inference, not a source. Learner pools (tanmedence) almost never have a published lane count and are mostly null by nature. The one place a secondary source asserts a lane count that could not be confirmed (Halassy Olivér, '6 sávos') it is recorded as hearsay in `notes` and the field is null.

THREE SCHEDULE ENCODINGS EXIST IN THE WILD, in descending order of usefulness to the app:

(1) HTML TABLE WITH AN INTEGER FREE-LANE COUNT — the jackpot, because the cell value IS the quantity the app needs. Three pools: Erzsébetligeti Rátonyi Gábor Uszoda (XVI), Szentmihályi Konrád Ferenc Uszoda (XVI) and Pesterzsébeti Uszoda (XX). The two XVI. kerület pools share an operator (Kertvárosi Sportlétesítményeket Üzemeltető Kft.) and a CMS, so ONE PARSER HANDLES BOTH: fetch '?content=dct&did=NN' where NN is found by scraping the nav for the anchor text 'Szabad pályák a közönségnek' (did=36 at Erzsébetliget, did=34 at Szentmihály — do not hardcode), skip the 4 chrome tables, select the table whose caption contains 'Közönség részére szabad sávok száma az úszómedencében', read columns H|K|Sz|Cs|P|Szo|V and 32 half-hour rows '6:00 - 6:30'..'21:00 - 21:30', and each cell is an integer count of free public lanes or 'X' for closed. Erzsébetliget additionally has a second table for the tanmedence whose cells are 'i'/blank (boolean, NOT a count); Szentmihály has no such table, so the parser must tolerate its absence.

Pesterzsébet (XX) is a DIFFERENT html-table shape and needs its own parser: server-rendered <table>s live at /melyvizes-medence/ and /tanmedence/ (the /savbeosztas/ page is only a chooser), six tables per page = Monday..Saturday with NO SUNDAY table even though the pool opens on Sundays, the header row enumerates '0.pálya'..'9.pálya' for the 10-lane deep pool and '5.pálya'..'1. pálya' (REVERSED) for the 5-lane tanmedence, an empty cell means free, and the words 'foglalt' / 'iskola' / 'iskolai-óvodai oktatás' mean occupied. CRITICAL GOTCHA: the cells use colspan, so naive <td> counting mis-aligns lanes.

(2) PDF GRID — seven pools, but in TWO FLAVOURS that must not be confused. The easier flavour is the Városgazda XVIII. Nonprofit Zrt. family (Bókay-park, Kastélydombi, Vilmos Endre), which shares ONE template across all three pools: URL pattern .../wp-content/uploads/<YYYY>/<MM>/<YYYY>-HL-{PU|KU|VE}-<YYYY>-<MONTH>-<start>-<end>.pdf, 2 pages (délelőtt / délután), A4 landscape, and a REAL TEXT LAYER that PyMuPDF reads directly — occupied cells carry both a fill colour AND the time-range text, free cells are white and empty, so colour decoding is optional here. Columns are 15-minute slots 6:00-12:45 and 13:00-20:45; rows are 7 day blocks x N lane rows (4 at Bókay and Kastélydomb, 6 at Vilmos Endre). Two gotchas: a coloured rectangle can span several lane rows vertically, and day names are stored letter-per-line and must be rejoined. Full-day closures appear as a purple band across all lanes.

The harder flavour is the rest (Újhegyi X, Csepeli Strandfürdő XXI, TVE Sportuszoda III, Csillaghegyi Árpád Forrásfürdő III), WHERE OCCUPANCY IS ENCODED PURELY AS CELL FILL COLOUR. These have NO usable text layer for the occupancy state: page.get_text() returns the day names, lane numbers and hour labels but the free/occupied state lives only in the rectangle fills. The working recipe is PyMuPDF — page.get_text('words') plus x/y bucketing to rebuild the grid, then page.get_drawings() to read each cell's fill RGB, then match those RGBs to the legend swatches printed on the page (and DROP the legend swatches themselves, which otherwise pollute the grid — at Újhegyi they sit at x0~16, x1~97, y~398-453). Exact observed RGB triples are recorded per pool in each scheduleSource.note so a scraper does not have to rediscover them. Two different semantics are in use: Újhegyi paints state directly (amber 1.0,0.75,0.0 = FOGLALT, green 0.0,0.69,0.31 = SZABAD), whereas Csepel paints the OCCUPYING CLUB's colour and leaves public slots unfilled, so free lanes = total lanes minus filled cells. Filenames encode the season and WILL change at the season turn — always scrape the parent 'Pályabeosztás' page for href$='.pdf' rather than hardcoding a URL.

(3) IMAGE (PNG/JPG) — two pools (Kispesti XIX, Hajós Alfréd Tanuszoda Budafok XXII). Kispest is the better of the two: a stable upload-path pattern .../wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/Savbeosztas-WEB-YYYY.MM.DD-MM.DD.png, two week panels, 'Medence 33 M' over 'Tanmedence', Sáv/Lane 1-6 per day (42 columns), hourly rows 06:00-21:00, GREEN = 'Lakosság számára elérhető', RED = 'Foglalt / Zárva'. These need OCR or manual transcription; treat as a weekly manual-refresh source.

AND THE REST PUBLISH NOTHING. Six pools are 'none-found' or 'facebook-only'. This is not always laziness on the operator's part — several genuinely allocate lanes only on a whiteboard at the ticket desk (Gazdagréti explicitly tells visitors to consult 'a jegypénztárnál elhelyezett foglaltsági tájékoztató').

TRAPS WORTH KNOWING. (a) Aggregator sites are wrong often enough to be dangerous: strand.hu gives Újhegyi's postcode as 1196, which is Kispest; the correct code is 1108. Always prefer OSM addr:* plus the operator's own contact page. (b) sport.ujbuda.hu (Nyéki Imre) is a Vite/React SPA serving a 2 KB JS shell — curl gets nothing. The content is reachable as JSON from https://api.ujbuda.hu/webapi/v1.0/static-pages/156 BUT ONLY with the header 'Domain: sport.ujbuda.hu'; without it the API answers {"error":{"code":10002,"message":"Invalid domain"}}. Resolve the numeric id from /webapi/v1.0/sitemap rather than hardcoding. (c) haloujpest.hu (Újpest) returns HTTP 403 with a JS 'Hitelesítés' anti-bot interstitial to every request regardless of headers — that pool is blocked, not schedule-less, and deserves a retry with a headless browser. www.varosgazda18.hu (the three XVIII. kerület pools) likewise returns 403 to curl and other scripted clients no matter what User-Agent is sent; its PDFs were only obtainable through a browser-like fetcher, so plan for a headless browser there too. (c2) esmtkuszoda-pesterzsebet.hu, the Pesterzsébet domain named in the brief, is DEAD — it now resolves to shared hosting whose TLS certificate covers unrelated domains; the live operator site is https://www.pesterzsebetiuszoda.hu/. (d) Several sites (uszodak16.hu, hegyvideksport.hu, sport13.hu, api.ujbuda.hu) intermittently return HTTP 000 / empty bodies; a 4x retry loop with a 3 s backoff fixed it. (e) A JPG named 'uszoda-palyarendszabalyok.jpg' on the BVSC site looks exactly like a lane schedule from its filename but is a trilingual spectator ground-rules poster — it was downloaded and viewed before being used, which is the only way to be sure. (f) Hungarian-language queries ('sávbeosztás', 'pályabeosztás', 'szabad pályák', 'vízfelület beosztás') find these pages; English ones do not.
